description: SEC-B-04 (ADR-TEXT-01): how untrusted text is shown on a decision surface (the approval card, its preview, its title, the reason's destination and source titles). Python (harness_core.security.display_safe), Node (domain/display-safe.ts) and the web client (lib/utils/display-safe.ts) each carry these tables as constants and replay every case; their tests fail when a table here and a table in code differ. 'identifier' text (an address, a channel, a host, a tool's name, a field name) marks every invisible, control or bidi character and every letter of a word that mixes scripts; 'prose' text (a message body) marks the same characters except a joiner or variation selector inside non-ASCII text, and keeps tab, newline and carriage return. In both, a URL's host and, in identifiers, an address's or a bare host's domain follow the host rule: a host that is mixed-script, whole-script confusable, or holds a letter that passes for an ASCII one is shown in punycode (the client shows the Unicode form beside it); any other host is shown in Unicode. Code points are hex.
destinationArgsRule: the arguments that say where a call's content goes (the worker's DESTINATION_ARGS and URL_ARGS): the card never cuts their value in its preview, so no recipient hides behind "Show all"
invisibleRule: a code point is invisible when it is in 'invisible', is a format character (general category Cf), or is a C0 or C1 control or DEL

proseKeeps.rule: in prose, a joiner is kept when the code points on both sides exist and are neither ASCII nor whitespace; a variation selector when the one before it exists and is neither ASCII nor whitespace

scriptRule: only letters (general category L) count; a letter in no range is script 'Other'; marks, digits, symbols and punctuation count for none
hostRule: each label: an xn-- label is decoded (one that does not decode leaves the host as written); a host whose labels are all ASCII is shown as written; else every label is NFKC-normalised and lower-cased, and the host is shown in Unicode only when every label holds only ASCII letters, digits and '-', and non-ASCII letters and marks, its letters' scripts are one script or within one allowed mix, it is not whole-script confusable (every letter in its script's lookalikes, and the last label in another script), and no Latin letter is in latinPassesForAscii or decomposes (NFD) to a mark in hiddenMarks. Otherwise each non-ASCII label is shown in punycode
